lessons.title: Must for Strong Obligation
lessons.content: 'Must' is used for strong personal obligations. It expresses something that is necessary or very important. The structure is Subject + must + V1.

details.explanation: 'Must' is used for obligations that come from yourself or are very important.
details.burmese: ငါ ဝိတ်ချရမယ်။

details.explanation: 'Must' is used for duties and responsibilities.
details.example: I must write a letter to John.
details.burmese: ငါ ဂျွန်ဆီ စာတစ်စောင် ရေးရမယ်။

details.explanation: 'Must' is used for important rules that must be followed.
details.example: Bicyclists must remember to signal when they turn.
details.burmese: စက်ဘီးစီးသူများ လှည့်တဲ့အခါ အမှတ်ပေးဖို့ မှတ်ထားရမယ်။

details.explanation: 'Must' is used for obligations related to exams and studies.
details.example: He must study harder if he wants to pass the exam.
details.burmese: သူ စာမေးပွဲ အောင်ချင်ရင် ပိုပြီး ကြိုးစားရမယ်။

lessons.title: Mustn't for Prohibition
lessons.content: 'Mustn't' (must not) is used to express that something is prohibited or not allowed. The structure is Subject + mustn't + V1.

details.explanation: 'Mustn't' is used for rules about transport safety.
details.example: Passengers mustn't talk to the driver.
details.burmese: ခရီးသည်များ ဒီရင်ဘောက် စကားမပြောခင်းမရပါ။
ရဲတပ်ဖွဲ့ဝင်များ တာဝန်ထမ်းဆောင်နေချိန်မှာ အရက်မသောက်ရပါ။

details.explanation: 'Mustn't' is used for rules about children.
details.burmese: ကလေးများ ဝါဂွမ်းမစားရပါ။

details.example: They mustn't use their mobile phones during lessons.
details.burmese: သူတို့ သင်ခန်းစာချိန်မှာ မိုဘိုင်းဖုန်းများ အသုံးမပြုရပါ။

lessons.title: Must in Questions
lessons.content: 'Must' can be used in questions to ask about obligation. The structure is Must + subject + V1?

details.explanation: 'Must' is used to ask if something is required.
details.example: Must I go to the party?

details.explanation: 'Must' is used to ask about the necessity of an action.
details.example: Must he make so much noise?
details.burmese: သူ ဆူညံစွာ လုပ်ရမလား။

lessons.title: Important Notes About Must
lessons.content: 'Must' is used only in the present and future. The past form of 'must' is 'had to'. 'Must' does not exist in the past tense.

details.explanation: 'Must' can only be used for present and future obligations.
details.example: I must finish this work before I leave.
details.burmese: ငါ ထွက်ခင် ဒီအလုပ်ကို ပြီးအောင်လုပ်ရမယ်။

details.explanation: For past obligations, use 'had to' instead of 'must'.
details.example: I had to finish the work yesterday. (Not: I musted finish)
details.burmese: ငါ မနေ့က ဒီအလုပ်ကို ပြီးအောင်လုပ်ရတယ်။
